new.title: Explore the Cité du design on the old arms factory
new.desc: The Cité du design occupies the former Manufacture d'armes, which made French army rifles for nearly 150 years until the early 2000s. Its main building, the Platine (about 200 x 32 m, by LIN architects), holds exhibition halls, libraries and a restaurant. Saint-Étienne is a UNESCO City of Design.
new.tip: Check current exhibitions on the official site before going; the Biennale takes over the site in spring of alternate years.
new.q: Cité du design, 3 rue Javelin Pagnon, Saint-Étienne

new.title: See modern art at the MAMC+ museum
new.desc: The Musée d'art moderne et contemporain de Saint-Étienne Métropole opened in 1987 as the first regional modern art museum in France. Its collection of nearly 23,000 works is mostly 20th-century, with design and photography, shown in about 3,000 m2 of galleries.
new.tip: Tram T1 or T3 stops at Musée Art Moderne; closed Tuesdays, and free on the first Sunday of the month and for under-26s per tourism listings.
new.q: Musée d'art moderne et contemporain, rue Fernand Léger, Saint-Priest-en-Jarez

new.title: Descend into the Puits Couriot mining museum
new.desc: The Parc-Musée de la Mine occupies the Couriot pit, which closed in 1973, on more than 8 hectares. A guide leads visitors through a reconstructed 400 m mine gallery, and the headframe walkway gives a view over the city.
new.tip: Allow about 1h15; the gallery is visited only with a guide. Bus line 7 or Clapier station are the nearest links.
new.q: Musée de la Mine - Puits Couriot, 3 boulevard Franchet d'Espèrey, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Tour the Chaudron and the Musée des Verts
new.desc: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard, nicknamed the Chaudron, is home to AS Saint-Étienne. The Musée des Verts inside is described as the first museum in France devoted to a single football club.
new.tip: Combined stadium tour plus museum tickets exist; closed on match days. Tram T3 stops at Stade Geoffroy-Guichard / Musée des Verts.
new.q: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard, 14 rue Paul et Pierre Guichard, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Trace bicycles, ribbons and rifles at the Musée d'art et d'industrie
new.desc: The museum is organised around three collections: arms, ribbons and cycles, all central to Saint-Étienne's industrial history. It notes that the first French bicycle was made in the city in 1886, and its ribbon collection is among the largest in the world.
new.tip: Open daily except Tuesday, roughly 10:00 to 18:00; tram T3 stop Bourse du travail is closest.
new.q: Musée d'art et d'industrie, 2 place Louis Comte, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Step inside Saint-Charles cathedral on Place Jean Jaurès
new.desc: The neo-Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Charles-Borromée was built from 1912 to 1923 and became a cathedral in 1970 when the diocese of Saint-Étienne was created. It was never completed: planned extra towers and a dome were not built.
new.tip: Entry is free; combine it with Place Jean Jaurès and the nearby pedestrian streets.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Charles, place Jean Jaurès, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Find the medieval Grand'Église, Forez Gothic
new.desc: The Grand'Église is an older parish church in Forez Gothic style, built most likely between 1450 and 1480. It recalls the medieval town that grew around it before the industrial boom.
new.tip: Free to enter; look at the Gothic vaults and then walk down toward Place du Peuple.
new.q: Grand'Église, place Boivin, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Climb the Jardin des Plantes for the city view
new.desc: This hillside garden in the city centre is also called the Chapeau Chinois for the conical roof of the opera house it contains. Terraces by the Maison de la Culture give a typical panorama of Saint-Étienne.
new.tip: Free and open every day; the upper alleys are best on a clear afternoon.
new.q: Jardin des Plantes, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Sit on Place du Peuple, the old market square
new.desc: Place du Peuple is one of the city's oldest squares, used as a market and gathering spot since the seventeenth century. It is still a commercial hub, ringed by cafés and shops.
new.tip: Free and always open; stop for a coffee on a terrace before heading to the markets.
new.q: Place du Peuple, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Walk the Le Corbusier site at Firminy
new.desc: Firminy-Vert holds a large Le Corbusier ensemble: Maison de la culture, stadium, swimming pool, Unité d'habitation and the Saint-Pierre church. The church was designed with José Oubrerie and finished in 2006, and the site is part of the UNESCO Le Corbusier listing.
new.tip: Guided visits of the Maison de la culture with the church, or of the Unité, take about 1h30 each.
new.q: Site Le Corbusier, Église Saint-Pierre, Firminy-Vert, Firminy

new.title: Visit the Collégiale Notre-Dame d'Espérance in Montbrison
new.desc: Founded in 1223 by Count Guy IV of Forez, this is described as the largest Gothic church in the Loire département. Its plan follows Lyon cathedral, and the apse holds the effigy of Guy IV.
new.tip: Free, open daily roughly 9:00 to 19:00 per tourism listings.
new.q: Collégiale Notre-Dame d'Espérance, 10 rue Notre-Dame, Montbrison

new.title: Tour the Renaissance Château de la Bâtie d'Urfé
new.desc: The château at Saint-Étienne-le-Molard keeps gardens in their 16th-century layout, restored by the Loire département since 1990. The interior opens only on guided tours, and summer shows run as the Nuits de la Bâtie d'Urfé.
new.tip: Plan about 90 minutes; the grounds can be visited freely, guided room tours cost extra.
new.q: Château de la Bastie d'Urfé, 1061 route de la Bâtie d'Urfé, Saint-Étienne-le-Molard

new.title: Explore the Benedictine abbey of Charlieu
new.desc: Founded in 875 and attached to Cluny until the end of the 18th century, Charlieu abbey is a major Romanesque site in northern Loire. Both free and guided visits are offered.
new.tip: Combined tickets exist with the Cordeliers convent at Saint-Nizier-sous-Charlieu; park on place des Bénédictins.
new.q: Abbaye bénédictine de Charlieu, place de l'Abbaye, Charlieu

new.title: Wander the Chartreuse village of Sainte-Croix-en-Jarez
new.desc: A former Carthusian monastery in the Pilat is now a lived-in village, recognised among the Plus beaux villages de France. Public areas are always open, while the kitchen, hermitage and medieval church are visited only with a guide.
new.tip: Free to stroll; guided visits run on afternoons and weekend mornings, so check the schedule.
new.q: Chartreuse de Sainte-Croix-en-Jarez, 4 place des Portes, Sainte-Croix-en-Jarez

new.title: Climb to Le Puy cathedral and its Romanesque cloister
new.desc: Notre-Dame-de-l'Annonciation is a UNESCO-listed cathedral and minor basilica since 1856, home to the Black Virgin and a cloister with a white, red and black diamond mosaic. Nave and choir are free; the cloister is part of a paid visit.
new.tip: The cloister is open daily from mid-May to mid-September; free entry on the first Sunday of the month from November to March.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame du Puy, rue des Tables, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Climb 268 steps to Saint-Michel d'Aiguilhe
new.desc: A Romanesque chapel crowns an 82 m volcanic needle at the edge of Le Puy, reached by 268 steps. Bishop Godelsalc is said to have commissioned it around 961, as pilgrimage toward Compostela was opening.
new.tip: Best early or late in the day to avoid crowds and for the light on the rock.
new.q: Chapelle Saint-Michel d'Aiguilhe, rue Saint-Michel, Aiguilhe

new.title: See the Saint-Joseph statue and basilica at Espaly
new.desc: A monumental Saint-Joseph statue about 22 m tall stands at the Espaly sanctuary, on the site of an older castle chapel. The rock gives a panorama over Le Puy-en-Velay.
new.tip: A marked trail (PR543) starts and ends in Espaly-Saint-Marcel; wear sturdy shoes.
new.q: Sanctuaire Saint-Joseph de Bon-Espoir, Espaly-Saint-Marcel

new.title: Wander the Jardin Henri Vinay and Musée Crozatier
new.desc: The 4.5 hectare Jardin Henri Vinay, laid out between 1825 and 1884, surrounds the Musée Crozatier, which holds art and archaeology of the Velay and Haute-Loire. It is a calm stop between the cathedral and the lower town.
new.tip: The garden opens about 7:15 to 19:00 or 20:00 depending on season, and entry is free.
new.q: Musée Crozatier, 2 rue Antoine Martin, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: See the Danse macabre at La Chaise-Dieu abbey
new.desc: The abbey church of Saint-Robert preserves a 15th-century Danse macabre fresco with pairs of corpses and living figures from each social rank. The abbey also hosts the classical-music Festival de La Chaise-Dieu, founded in 1966.
new.tip: Free to look around the church; the festival takes place around the end of August.
new.q: Abbatiale Saint-Robert, place de l'Écho, La Chaise-Dieu

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Polignac fortress
new.desc: Polignac fortress sits on a volcanic rock above the village, with a keep about 32 m tall and nearly 3 hectares of ramparts. From the top there are views over the Velay and the Meygal.
new.tip: Open from about February to early January with seasonal hours; allow around 1h30.
new.q: Forteresse de Polignac, Polignac

new.title: Visit Château de Lavoûte-Polignac above the Loire
new.desc: The château on a rocky spur above a bend of the Loire is described as one of the first pleasure châteaux on the river, and is still held by the Polignac family. A date of 1634 and the family arms appear above the south door.
new.tip: Visits are guided; hours were given as 10:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, so check ahead.
new.q: Château de Lavoûte-Polignac, Lavoûte-sur-Loire

new.title: Count the carved capitals of Brioude basilica
new.desc: Saint-Julien is often called the largest Romanesque church in Auvergne, with about 500 sculpted capitals and a 74 m length. A sanctuary has stood over the tomb of the martyr Julian since the late 4th century.
new.tip: Free entry; the exterior corbels of the east end are among its best details.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Julien, place Grégoire de Tours, Brioude

new.title: Discover the cloister of Lavaudieu abbey
new.desc: Lavaudieu's Romanesque cloister is described as the only one preserved in Auvergne, with wooden upper galleries; the refectory holds a large fresco of Christ with the apostles. The village is among the Plus beaux villages de France.
new.tip: Walk over the 12th-century bridge on the Senouire for the classic view.
new.q: Abbaye Saint-André, Lavaudieu

new.title: See the natural Pont d'Arc arch over the Ardèche
new.desc: The Pont d'Arc is a natural stone bridge across the Ardèche river, a protected site since 1931 according to Wikipedia. It marks the entrance of the Gorges de l'Ardèche, and the Chauvet cave lies close by.
new.tip: Free viewpoint near Vallon-Pont-d'Arc; best in morning light, or from a canoe.
new.q: Pont d'Arc, route des Gorges de l'Ardèche, Vallon-Pont-d'Arc

new.title: Enter the Grotte Chauvet 2 replica cave
new.desc: Grotte Chauvet 2 is a full-scale replica of the original Chauvet cave, opened in 2015 about five kilometres from the real site. Guided groups of up to 25 see paintings about 30,000 years old over around 50 minutes.
new.tip: Booking is required; tickets can include the Cité de la Préhistoire at Orgnac. The cave is wheelchair accessible.
new.q: Grotte Chauvet 2 Ardèche, 4941 route de Bourg-Saint-Andéol, Vallon-Pont-d'Arc

new.title: Stroll cliff-top Balazuc, a Plus beau village
new.desc: Balazuc perches on a cliff above the Ardèche and belongs to Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The 14th-century Tour de la Reine Jeanne faces the village, which also has the Muséum de l'Ardèche.
new.tip: Free to wander; go early in summer when the lanes get busy.
new.q: Balazuc village, Balazuc

new.title: Visit Vogüé below its four-tower château
new.desc: Vogüé is built in an amphitheatre against a cliff on the Ardèche, dominated by a château with four corner towers. It carries the Plus Beaux Villages de France label and has the very narrow Rue des Puces.
new.tip: Free to wander; it is also a start point for river descents.
new.q: Château de Vogüé, Vogüé

new.title: Descend 121 m into the Aven d'Orgnac
new.desc: The Aven d'Orgnac is a Grand Site de France since 2004, a huge cavern visited with a guide down to 121 m at about 12 C. The Cité de la Préhistoire museum at the surface covers Ardèche prehistory.
new.tip: The cave visit lasts about an hour with many steps; bring a jacket.
new.q: Aven d'Orgnac, 2240 route de l'Aven, Orgnac-l'Aven

new.title: Trace the Montgolfier balloon story at the Vidalon paper mills
new.desc: The Musée des Papeteries Canson et Montgolfier sits in the birthplace of the Montgolfier brothers, with a memorial to the first flight made at Vidalon on 14 December 1782. The buildings have been listed since 2012.
new.tip: Open July and August 14:15 to 18:00 daily, otherwise Wednesday and Sunday afternoons; confirm before going.
new.q: Musée des Papeteries Canson et Montgolfier, 700 rue de Vidalon, Davézieux

new.title: Take in the Rhône from the Tournon château terraces
new.desc: The Château-musée de Tournon stands on a rock above the Rhône and has housed the Rhône Museum's collections since 1928. Two terraces give a panorama across to Tain-l'Hermitage and the Hermitage vineyards.
new.tip: Cross the Marc Seguin footbridge to Tain for the best view back to the château.
new.q: Château-Musée de Tournon, Tournon-sur-Rhône

new.title: Grab a lunch gandot at Gandot
new.desc: Restaurant Gandot is named after the miners' lunchbox and serves fresh pasta made on site, vegan salads and all-in-one dishes in eco-friendly packaging. Daily menus cost about 8.50 to 11.20 euros.
new.tip: Weekday daytime only (about 9:00 to 17:00), closed at weekends; check before going.
new.q: Gandot, 6 rue Aristide Briand et de la Paix, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Dine at the brasserie La Loco, Maître Restaurateur
new.desc: La Loco is a brasserie holding the Maître Restaurateur label for fresh traditional cooking, rated about 4.4 on large review samples.
new.tip: Closed Saturday per tourism listings; book for dinner.
new.q: La Loco, 29 avenue Denfert-Rochereau, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Taste a praluline at Pralus on rue Michelet
new.desc: Pralus's Saint-Étienne shop has sold the praluline, a brioche studded with pink pralines, since 2017. The praluline was created in Roanne by Auguste Pralus in the mid-1950s per the house's own history.
new.tip: Buy a slice of praluline to eat on the go.
new.q: Pralus, 9 rue Michelet, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Try sarasson at Au Matefaim in the Halles Mazerat
new.desc: Au Matefaim is a lunch counter and deli in the Halles Mazerat selling Auvergne cheeses, Duculty salt meats and sarasson du Forez, a fresh cheese local to the area.
new.tip: Closed Mondays with the market; ask for a plate with sarasson and cured meats.
new.q: Au Matefaim, Halles Mazerat, 2 cours Victor Hugo, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Order snails at L'Escargot d'Or
new.desc: This traditional restaurant opposite the covered market is known for Burgundy snails served as a feuillantin in poivrade sauce, plus foie gras. Reviews average about 4.3 from roughly 1,600 Google ratings.
new.tip: Mid-range prices; book for dinner.
new.q: L'Escargot d'Or, 5 cours Victor Hugo, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Sip hot chocolate at Les Ateliers Weiss
new.desc: The Weiss chocolate house combines a shop, a hot-chocolate counter, exhibitions and a museum on the city's chocolate history. The workshop tours opened to visitors in 2016.
new.tip: Open Monday to Saturday about 9:00 to 19:00; the factory walkway may be closed, so confirm.
new.q: Les Ateliers Weiss, 1 rue Eugène Weiss, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Book a table at Maison Troisgros in Ouches
new.desc: Maison Troisgros, Le Bois sans Feuilles, holds three Michelin stars and has been three-starred since 1968. It moved from Roanne to Ouches in 2017 and is now run by César Troisgros.
new.tip: Reserve long in advance; address is 728 route de Villerest.
new.q: Maison Troisgros, 728 route de Villerest, Ouches

new.title: Lunch at Le Central, the Troisgros café-épicerie in Roanne
new.desc: Opened in 1996 by Michel and Marie-Pierre Troisgros, Le Central is a café-épicerie in central Roanne with a bistro menu and a grocery of sauces and conserves.
new.tip: Sources disagree on the address, so confirm on the official site; lunch is the easier slot.
new.q: Le Central, cours de la République, Roanne

new.title: Buy the original praluline at Pralus on rue Charles de Gaulle
new.desc: The first Pralus shop in Roanne opened in 1948, and the praluline brioche was created in this town. A second shop stands at the Halles Diderot.
new.tip: Buy a whole praluline or a slice; the Halles shop is closed Mondays.
new.q: Pralus, 8 rue Charles de Gaulle, Roanne

new.title: Eat at Le Bouchon des Halles in Roanne
new.desc: Le Bouchon des Halles is a restaurant in the Halles Diderot, Roanne's covered gourmet market where the Mons brothers opened their first store in 1983.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; go at lunch among the stalls.
new.q: Le Bouchon des Halles, Halles Diderot, rue Diderot, Roanne

new.title: Dine at one-star Le Chamarlenc in Le Puy
new.desc: Le Chamarlenc, opened in 2023 by chef Yoan Delorme, holds a Michelin star for creative cuisine and scores 13.5 in Gault&Millau. Indicative prices run 47 to 96 euros without drinks.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; it is on rue Raphaël, close to the lace centre.
new.q: Le Chamarlenc, 19 rue Raphaël, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Taste Puy lentils and verveine at L'Émotion
new.desc: L'Émotion on place Cadelade is a gourmet restaurant working with local products such as Puy lentils, verveine verte and black Velay lamb. Its Petit Futé rating is 4.6 from 90 reviews.
new.tip: Check recent reviews; one from March 2024 questioned value for money.
new.q: L'Émotion, 15 place Cadelade, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Taste verveine du Velay at the Pagès distillery
new.desc: The verbena liqueur of the Velay dates to 1859. The Pagès distillery runs guided visits ending in a tasting, and the firm is a Living Heritage Company.
new.tip: Check opening and booking with the distillery; closed on 1 November and 25 December.
new.q: Distillerie Pagès, 202 avenue René Descartes, Saint-Germain-Laprade

new.title: Taste Saint-Joseph wine at Cave de Saint-Désirat
new.desc: Founded in 1960, this cooperative represents about 40 percent of the Saint-Joseph appellation and also bottles Condrieu and Crozes-Hermitage. Visits include a guided tour and an olfactory course before tasting.
new.tip: Check opening hours; a walk starts nearby at Rochevine.
new.q: Cave de Saint-Désirat, 8 quartier Tine Rodet, Saint-Désirat

new.title: Have a farm snack at the Source de la Loire café
new.desc: A farm café-restaurant stands at Mont Gerbier de Jonc, where one of the three springs of the Loire flows into a stone basin in the former stable.
new.tip: Seasonal hours; open roughly mid-March to mid-November.
new.q: Ferme Café Restaurant La Source de la Loire, Mont Gerbier de Jonc, Sainte-Eulalie

new.title: Taste Picodon at Terra Cabra in Planzolles
new.desc: Terra Cabra is a farm and maturing workshop in the Ardèche Cévennes where a 50-minute visit ends with tasting goat cheeses of different ages up to Picodon AOP.
new.tip: Reserve a visit; offered in several languages.
new.q: Terra Cabra - Peytot, ferme et atelier d'affinage, Quartier de l'Église, Planzolles

new.title: Buy Picodon at the high-altitude Oppidum farm
new.desc: This organic farm at 1,000 m in Saint-Andéol-de-Fourchades keeps 70 Alpine chamois goats and sells AOP Picodon on site, with guided tours.
new.tip: Ask about tours in advance.
new.q: Ferme de l'Oppidum, Saint-Andéol-de-Fourchades

new.title: Stop at Auberge de Bachasson below Gerbier de Jonc
new.desc: The Auberge de Bachasson stands about 800 m from Mont Gerbier de Jonc and serves local mountain cooking.
new.tip: Check opening times; popular with hikers.
new.q: Auberge de Bachasson, Sainte-Eulalie

new.title: Order Puy lentils at La Taverne on place Cadelade
new.desc: La Taverne offers a ham-knuckle dish with Lentilles vertes du Puy AOP and a dessert with verveine soufflé glacé and lentil crisp, according to its 2025 group menu.
new.tip: Check the current menu before going.
new.q: La Taverne, place Cadelade, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Climb the Crêt de Roc steps for rooftop views
new.desc: The Montée du Crêt de Roc is an urban staircase, freely accessible, with a panoramic view over the city roofs.
new.tip: Wear proper shoes and expect an effort.
new.q: Montée du Crêt de Roc, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Hike Parc de Montaud to Crêt des 6 Soleils
new.desc: The Crêt des Soleils at the top of Parc de Montaud gives a 360-degree view over Saint-Étienne. A Boucle verte route runs on to Puits Couriot.
new.tip: A short loop is about 3 km; return by public transport from La Terrasse.
new.q: Parc de Montaud, 18 rue Benoît Frachon, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Browse rue des Martyrs-de-Vingré
new.desc: This pedestrian street has a village feel with shops, terraces and restaurants, in the heart of the centre. It is free to walk at any time.
new.tip: Visit in the early evening for the terraces.
new.q: Rue des Martyrs-de-Vingré, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Join the Biennale Internationale Design
new.desc: Launched in 1998, the Biennale takes place at the Cité du design in spring of alternate years. The 14th edition is planned for 26 April to 30 May 2027 (dates provisional).
new.tip: Confirm dates on biennale-design.com.
new.q: Cité du design, 3 rue Javelin Pagnon, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Browse the Halles Mazerat market hall
new.desc: The Halles Mazerat is the city's covered market, with stalls selling cheese, charcuterie and prepared dishes. It is closed on Mondays.
new.tip: Go in the morning for the best choice.
new.q: Halles Mazerat, cours Victor Hugo, Saint-Étienne

new.title: Paddle the Gorges de l'Ardèche under the Pont d'Arc
new.desc: Canoe descents start at Vallon-Pont-d'Arc, from 8 km to the full 32 km, passing under the Pont d'Arc between cliffs up to 300 m. Operators run trips from early April to late October with shuttle included.
new.tip: Prices run from about 18 euros for 8 km; you should be able to swim 25 m.
new.q: Descente des gorges de l'Ardèche, Vallon-Pont-d'Arc

new.title: Ride the Mastrou steam train from Tournon
new.desc: The Chemin de fer du Vivarais runs a 33 km metre-gauge line between Tournon and Lamastre, built 1886 to 1891 and reopened in 1969 by volunteers. Steam locomotives from 1902 to 1932 are used.
new.tip: Reservation is recommended; check the current timetable at trainardeche.fr.
new.q: Train de l'Ardèche, 111 route du Grand Pont, Saint-Jean-de-Muzols

new.title: Ride a vélorail through the Gorges du Doux
new.desc: The vélorail at Boucieu-le-Roi uses the old Vivarais line. A railcar takes you up and you pedal back down, for example on the 8 km Châtaigniers route.
new.tip: Combined train and vélorail tickets exist.
new.q: Vélorail des Gorges du Doux, Gare de Boucieu-le-Roi, route du pont du Roi, Boucieu-le-Roi

new.title: Swim and walk around the volcanic Lac du Bouchet
new.desc: This circular maar lake in Haute-Loire has a Pavillon Bleu beach and a 3 km loop trail. Lifeguards supervise swimming daily from the second week of July to the end of August.
new.tip: Free access; the water is cold.
new.q: Lac du Bouchet, Cayres

new.title: Walk or swim at Lac d'Issarlès
new.desc: A volcanic lake with a 3.5 km loop and a summer nautical base renting canoes, paddleboards and pedal boats. Supervised swimming runs July and August.
new.tip: The level can drop outside season; dogs are allowed on a lead outside the swimming zone.
new.q: Lac d'Issarlès, Le Lac-d'Issarlès

new.title: Climb Mont Gerbier de Jonc by the Loire sources
new.desc: Mont Gerbier de Jonc is a volcanic cone, with the Loire's three springs at its foot in Sainte-Eulalie at about 1,408 m.
new.tip: Free; the site is accessible all year.
new.q: Mont Gerbier de Jonc, Sainte-Eulalie

new.title: Hike to the Crêt de la Perdrix, summit of the Pilat
new.desc: The Crêt de la Perdrix is the highest point of the Pilat massif at 1,432 m, with views reaching the Alps. Loops link it with the Crêt de l'Œillon.
new.tip: Park near La Jasserie; snow can close the upper road.
new.q: Crêt de la Perdrix, parking de la Jasserie, Le Bessat

new.title: Walk to the Saut du Gier waterfall
new.desc: A short loop of about 3 km leads to the Saut du Gier cascade from La Valla-en-Gier, without particular difficulty.
new.tip: Some paths between La Jasserie and the falls were closed, so check trail status.
new.q: Cascade du Saut du Gier, La Valla-en-Gier

new.title: Start the Via Podiensis with the pilgrim blessing in Le Puy
new.desc: Pilgrims receive a blessing at Notre-Dame cathedral, collect their credential, then leave by the cathedral steps where bronze nails mark the GR65 toward Compostela.
new.tip: Mass at 7:00 daily from April to October.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame du Puy, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Hear classical music at the Festival de La Chaise-Dieu
new.desc: Founded in 1966, this classical and sacred music festival is held mainly in the abbey church around the end of August.
new.tip: Check dates and book on the festival site.
new.q: Abbatiale Saint-Robert, La Chaise-Dieu

new.title: Follow the Badoit trail in Saint-Galmier
new.desc: A 1h30 guided walk starts at the Badoit kiosk or the tourist office, and the Fontfort spring was bought by Auguste Saturnin Badoit in 1837. A bottling plant tour exists by reservation.
new.tip: Steep slopes and stairs; book ahead.
new.q: Kiosque Badoit, Saint-Galmier

new.title: Shop the Saturday market in Tournon-sur-Rhône
new.desc: The grand marché runs on Saturday mornings from 7:00 to 13:00 under the halle on place Jean Jaurès, with 45 to 50 stalls.
new.tip: Arrive early for the best produce.
new.q: Halle, place Jean Jaurès, Tournon-sur-Rhône

new.title: Browse the Tuesday and Friday market in Roanne
new.desc: The Place du Marché in Roanne hosts markets every Tuesday and Friday morning.
new.tip: Combine it with the Halles Diderot.
new.q: Place du Marché, Roanne

new.title: Watch the Source Intermittente geyser in Vals-les-Bains
new.desc: In Vals-les-Bains a natural geyser rises about four times a day, pushed by CO2 from a deep borehole.
new.tip: Winter times were listed as 4:30, 10:30, 16:30 and 22:30; confirm locally.
new.q: Source Intermittente, Vals-les-Bains

new.title: Drive the D290 Ardèche gorges belvederes
new.desc: The D290 runs about 29 km from Vallon-Pont-d'Arc to Saint-Martin-d'Ardèche with 11 viewpoints, including Serre de Tourre above the Pas de Mousse meander and Gournier.
new.tip: Free; for the Madeleine belvedere walk about 500 m on a footpath.
new.q: Belvédère du Serre de Tourre, route des Gorges, Saint-Remèze

new.title: Visit Antraigues and the Maison Jean Ferrat
new.desc: Jean Ferrat adopted this village in 1964 and wrote La Montagne there. The Maison-Musée Jean Ferrat is on place de la Résistance and his grave is on local walking routes.
new.tip: The Jean Ferrat festival runs in July.
new.q: Maison Jean Ferrat, place de la Résistance, Antraigues-sur-Volane

new.title: Watch bobbin lace demonstrations at the Le Puy lace centre
new.desc: The Centre d'Enseignement de la Dentelle au Fuseau, founded in 1974, teaches bobbin lace and sells lace on site. Demonstrations are held on weekdays at 10:30, 14:30 and 15:30.
new.tip: Saturday by appointment only.
new.q: Centre d'Enseignement de la Dentelle au Fuseau, 38-44 rue Raphaël, Le Puy-en-Velay

new.title: Join a Castagnade chestnut festival in the Monts d'Ardèche
new.desc: The Castagnades des Monts d'Ardèche are chestnut festivals across 11 villages, from Désaignes to Joyeuse, with producer markets; the 2026 edition marked 20 years of the Châtaigne d'Ardèche AOP.
new.tip: Held in October and early November.
new.q: Joyeuse, Ardèche

new.title: Walk around Lac de Saint-Front, a high crater lake
new.desc: Lac de Saint-Front is a round crater lake formed by a violent volcanic explosion, with loops through pine and beech woods.
new.tip: Check swimming rules locally.
new.q: Lac de Saint-Front, Saint-Front
